title: Science of Love
text:
I do not know. Only in the spring

of your eyes there reaches me the gloomy news

of God; only on your lips, the caress

of a world in harvest, of a celestial granary.


Are you clean crystal, or a destroying

snowfield? No, I do not know... Of this delight,

I know only its cosmic greed,

the sidereal beating with which I love you.


I do not know whether you are death or life,

whether I touch rose in you, whether I touch star,

whether I call God or you when I call you.


Reed in the water or deaf wounded stone,

I know only that the afternoon is wide and beautiful,

I know only that I am a man and that I love you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's claimed ignorance and its cosmic account of embodied love.

title: Man Is Love. Man Is a Beam, a Center...
text:
Man is love. Man is a beam, a center

where the world is knotted. If Man fails,

again come the void and the battle

of first chaos and the God who cries, "I enter!"


Man is love, and God lives within

that deep chest, and there falls silent;

with those eyes he peers, beyond the fence,

at his creation, astonished by encounter.


I, Love-Man, govern the total system

(my Universe). Oh God, do not annihilate me,

you immense flower growing in my insomnia!


I am your center for you, your theme

of deep rumination, your dwelling and your hanging gardens.

If I come undone, you disappear.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Alonso's daring mutual dependence between human consciousness and God.

title: Friends Who Forever...
text:
Friends who forever

left us,


dear friends forever gone,

outside Time

and outside Space!


For the soul nourished on sorrows,

for the pierced heart, perhaps.
editorial_note: The translation follows the short Spanish fragment as an elegy for friends beyond time and space.

title: To Elizabeth
text:
Do you wish to be loved? Then do not lose

the course of your heart. Only what

you are must you be, and what you are not, no.

Thus, in the world, your subtle manner, your grace,

your most beautiful being, will be the object of endless praise,

and love, a simple duty.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Spanish catalog's advice-like phrasing and compact moral turn.

editorial_note: This variant keeps the same English rendering as 'To Elizabeth' while preserving the catalog's first-line title.
